SPECIFICATION FOR HANDLOOM COTTON SPONGE CLOTH, GREY, STRIPED OR CHECKED

( First Revision)
0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 11 May 1987, after the draft finalized by the Handloom and Khadi Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Divjsion Couccil. 0.2 This standard, first published in 1956, has been revised in order to make it up-to-date in respect of the following changes: a) Yarn conforming to IS : 171-1985* has been recommended; b) ffPdUIeson inspection, marking and packing have been included; c) Latest versions of Indian Standards on test methods have been sp:cilicd, 0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2- 1960t. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 1, SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the constructional particulars and other requirements of three varieties of handloom cotton spooge cloth, grey, striped or checked. *Spedflcation for cotton and ootlon regenerated collulosio fibroblondodprey yarn ( third rcvlslon ). tRulor for rounding oB numerical valuom ( ruvlJrd).

1.2 This standard does not specify the general appearance, finish or colour and their combination in striped or checked

lustre, feel, cloth.

2. MANUFACTURE 2.1 Yarn - The cotton yarn used in the manufacture conform to the requirements of IS : 171-1985*. 2.1.1 The warp yarn shall not be sized before weaving. 2.2 Cloth - Each cut ecd of the sponge cloth shall be hemmed to a depth of not less than 1 cm, the raw edges having a turn in of 10 mm Cotton sewing thread conforming to variety before the hem is formed. number 31 of IS : 1720-1978t shall be used iu hemming and nunlber of stitches shall be at least 40 per decimetre. 3. REQUIREMENTS 3.1 The cloth shall conform to the constructional characteristics as given in Tables 1 and 2. requirements and other of cloth shall

3.2 If in order to ilIustrate or specify the indeterminable characteristics, such as general appearance, lustre, feel, and shade of the cloth, a sample has been agreed upon and sealed, the supply shall be in conformity with the sample in such respects. 3.2.1 The custody of the sealed sample shall be a matter agreement between the buyer and the seller. 4. 5. MARKING 5.1 The cloth shall be suitably marked or labelled with the following informati0U: 8) Name of the material, and variety number; b) Manufacturer's name, initials or trade-mark; c) Month and year of manufacture; and d) Length and width of piece, *Glossaryof terms pertaining to dofocts in fubrics, 6

IS : 860 - 1987
51.1

The cloth may also be marked

with the Standard

Mark.

The use of Ihe Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the NOTE Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Stacdard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers, may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

6.

PACKING

6.1 Unless otherwise agreed upon by the buyer and the seller, the cloth shall preferably be packed in bales or cases in conformity with the procedure laid down either in IS : 1347-1972* or IS : 293-19803. 7. SAMPLING 7.1 The scale of sampling and criteria for conformity as given in IS : 3919-19661 shall be followed in respect of physical characteristics, nameiy, ends and picks, weight, length, width, and weave. 7.2 The scale of sampling and criteria for conformity as given in IS : 5463-1969s shall be followed in respect of the chemical requirements of colour fastness and scouring loss.
